input: This memo recommends that a three-month pilot of condition sensors be carried out on 19 pumps, and that the reliability engineering group should own the pilot. The decision on whether to proceed with a full installation is to be held until the results of the pilot have been reported, and the pilot will report before the March capital review. Maintenance records covering a period of 12 months show a total of 1357 h of unplanned downtime across the 180 pumps that are in operation at the plant, and it is notable that bearing failures account for 38% of these downtime hours. A sensor set covering all 180 pumps has been quoted at $389k installed, plus $68k per year. In a trial conducted by the vendor on a comparable unit, the sensors were found to cut downtime by 21%, although it should be emphasised that this figure is a vendor figure and has not been measured at this plant. The pilot itself will cost $40k over the three months. The downtime that the pilot needs to address is concentrated in bearing failures, which is precisely the class of failure that the sensors are designed to detect, and the pilot will measure the downtime on its pumps against the records base set out above. Spare-part lead times will remain unchanged by the sensors, and no part of the case depends on repairs being carried out more quickly: the benefit, if the pilot confirms one, will come from receiving warning before a failure occurs, rather than from shorter outages.
